answer_style.title: Answer Style Guidelines
answer_style.content: Keep answers concise and actionable. Use bullet points for plans. Include specific numbers (calories, grams, reps) when available from user context. Prefer practical suggestions over theory.

nutrition.title: Balanced Meal Basics
nutrition.content: A balanced meal includes a protein source (20-30g), complex carbs, healthy fats, and vegetables. Aim for 400-600 calories per main meal depending on daily calorie goal.

nutrition.title: Indian Meal Options
nutrition.content: Popular Indian meals: Dal + roti (400 cal), Rajma chawal (500 cal), Paneer sabzi + roti (450 cal), Idli sambar (300 cal), Poha (250 cal). These are filling and nutritionally complete.

workout.title: Beginner Workout Structure
workout.content: Beginners: 3 days/week full-body workouts. Each session: 5 min warm-up, 3 sets of 8-12 reps for compound movements (squats, push-ups, rows), 5 min cool-down.

workout.title: Home Workout Essentials
workout.content: Effective home exercises: Push-ups (chest/triceps), Squats (legs), Planks (core), Lunges (legs/glutes), Mountain climbers (cardio+core). No equipment needed.

bmi.title: BMI Interpretation
bmi.content: BMI ranges: Under 18.5 = underweight, 18.5-24.9 = normal, 25-29.9 = overweight, 30+ = obese. BMI is a screening tool, not a diagnosis — muscle mass and body composition matter too.
